chunks: He has the keys of the Unknown. No one but He has knowledge; He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls without His knowledge, nor a grain in the darkest (recess) of the earth, nor any thing green or seared that is not recorded in the open book (of nature).
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about Allah's knowledge of the unseen and natural details?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to establish the foundation of divine omniscience, which underpins the concept of 'Adl (Divine Justice) and the precise recording of human deeds. The mention of 'keys to the unseen' (Mafatih al-Ghayb) is interpreted not just as exclusive knowledge, but as the source of all potentiality, linking the microcosm of falling leaves to the macrocosm of cosmic order. This comprehensive awareness ensures that no action, however small, is lost, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the meticulous accounting of the soul in the Hereafter.
